Becau{{ls}}e you can not heare my vvord. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=44}} You are of your father the Diuel, and the de{{ls}}ires of your father you vvil doe. he vvas a {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ S. If I {{ls}}ay the veritie: vvhy doe you not beleeue me? {{verse|chapter=8|verse=47}} {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Go{{ls}}pel vpō {{sc|Passion}} Sunday.}}He that is of God, heareth the vvordes of God. Therfore you heare not, becau{{ls}}e you are not of God. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=48}} The Iewes therfore an{{ls}}vvered, and {{ls}}aid to him, Doe not we {{ls}}ay vvel that thou art a Samaritane, and ha{{ls}}t a diuil? {{verse|chapter=8|verse=49}} {{sc|Iesvs}} an{{ls}}vvered, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ He denieth not that he is a Samaritane, becau{{ls}}e he is our keeper or protector, as the vvord {{ls}}ignifieth, and becau{{ls}}e he is in deede that merciful Samaritane in the parable of the wounded man Luc. 10, 33. ''Aug. tract. 43 in Ioan''.}}∷ I haue no deuil: but I doe honour my Father, and you haue di{{ls}}honoured me. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=50}} but I {{ls}}eeke not mine ovvne glorie. there is that {{ls}}eeketh and iudgeth.

{{verse|chapter=8|verse=51}} Amen, amen I {{ls}}ay to you, If any man keepe my vvord, he {{ls}}hal not {{ls}}ee death for euer. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=52}} The Ievves therfore {{ls}}aid, Now vve haue knovven that thou ha{{ls}}t a deuil. Abraham is dead, and the Prophets: and thou {{ls}}aie{{ls}}t, If any man keepe my vvord, he {{ls}}hal not ta{{ls}}t death for euer. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=53}} VVhy, art thou greater then our father Abraham, vvho is dead? and the Prophets are dead. VVhom doe{{ls}}t thou make thy {{ls}}elf? {{verse|chapter=8|verse=54}} {{sc|Iesvs}} an{{ls}}wered, If I doe glorifie my {{ls}}elf, my glorie is nothing. it is my father that glorifieth me, vvhom you {{ls}}ay that he is your God. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=55}} And you haue not knovven him, but I knovv him. And if I {{ls}}hal {{ls}}ay that I knovv him not: I {{ls}}hal be like to you, a lyer. But I doe knovv him, and doe keepe his vvord. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=56}} Abraham your father reioyced that he might {{ls}}ee my day: and he {{ls}}avv, and vvas glad. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=57}} The Ievves therfore {{ls}}aid to him, Thou ha{{ls}}t not yet fiftie yeres, and ha{{ls}}t thou {{ls}}een Abraham? {{verse|chapter=8|verse=58}} {{sc|Iesvs}} {{ls}}aid to them, Amen, amen I {{ls}}ay to you, before that Abraham vvas made, I am. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=59}} They tooke {{ls}}tones therfore to ca{{ls}}t at him. but {{sc|Iesvs}} hid him {{ls}}elf, and vvent out of the temple.⊣
